Glossary

Source: vignettes/articles/glossary.Rmd
glossary.Rmd

Short definitions of the terms that trip up new readers of SRTR data, each with a link to the guide that explains it. Start with the identifiers: which one you count decides what your numbers mean.

Identifiers: what each one counts

Identifier One per Watch for
PX_ID Waitlist registration One person can be listed more than once, at several centers or for several organs.
PERS_ID Person A person transplanted twice has two transplant registrations. The donor files also hold a PERS_ID, with its own meaning.
TRR_ID Transplant registration Repeats on every follow-up form for that transplant.
TX_ID Transplant event Shared by the registrations of one multi-organ transplant, which can sit in several organ files.
TRR_FOL_ID Follow-up form Several per transplant registration.
DONOR_ID Donor One deceased donor can give organs to several recipients.
CTR_ID Center Transplant files hold center identifiers such as REC_CTR_ID.

These roles come from the variable labels in the SRTR data dictionary, which are not always consistent, so check a key on your own files before joining on it. See What are you counting? and Transplants are not people.

Files and releases

SAF (standard analysis file). One of the files SRTR delivers to researchers, such as TX_KI. sRtr calls the name a file key. See Getting started.

Release. A delivery of SAFs, named by year and month: "2303" is the March 2023 release. Variables are added and dropped between releases. See Releases.

File names. The first part says what the file holds and the second says the organ:

  • CAND_ waitlist candidates, STATHIST_ waitlist status history, TX_ transplants, TXF_ transplant follow-up forms; DONOR_DECEASED and DONOR_LIVE donors.
  • Organs: KI kidney, LI liver, PA pancreas, KP kidney-pancreas, HR heart, LU lung, HL heart-lung, IN intestine. Candidate and status files group organs: KIPA (kidney and pancreas), LIIN (liver and intestine), THOR (thoracic: heart and lung).

See Organs and multi-organ transplants.

Data dictionary. SRTR’s published list of every variable, its label and its format. sRtr ships copies as dictionary and dictionary_versions. See Releases, the data dictionary and warnings.

Codes and missing values

Format. The code list that gives a variable’s values their meaning, such as 1 for “Yes”. The same code can mean different things in different formats. See Labels and codes.

Code in no format. A value in your file that the dictionary’s format does not list. sRtr keeps it and warns. See Codes in no format.

Unknown, not done, not applicable. Different kinds of missing value, each with its own codes. Once they all become NA, they look the same. See What the codes mean and Choosing what becomes NA.

Dates and outcomes

Transplant date (REC_TX_DT). Where post-transplant time starts.

Last follow-up date (TFL_LAFUDATE, “last graft follow up date”). The last date the transplant was known to be followed, where follow-up of the graft ends. See Whose follow-up?

Graft failure date (TFL_GRAFT_DT). See Graft failure and death on the same day.

Death dates. Three sources: the OPTN death date (PERS_OPTN_DEATH_DT), the Social Security death date (PERS_SSA_DEATH_DT) and the date on the follow-up forms (TFL_DEATH_DT). A composite death date takes the first available in a fixed order. See Which death date?

Follow-up form date (TFL_PX_STAT_DT). The date of the form that reported an event, not the date the event began. See A form date is not an onset date.

Listing date (CAN_LISTING_DT). When a candidate was added to the waiting list; it does not change when the listing is transferred.

Risk scores

KDRI and KDPI (kidney donor risk index and profile index), EPTS (estimated post-transplant survival), LKDPI (living kidney donor profile index), PDRI (pancreas donor risk index), donor eGFR (estimated kidney function) and PVR (pulmonary vascular resistance). Each is added by an add_*() function. See The scores.

Organizations and rules

SRTR. The Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients, which analyzes the national transplant data and distributes the SAFs.

OPTN. The Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network, which collects the data and sets allocation policy. Its regions are mapped by get_hrsa_optn_regions(). UNOS has operated the OPTN.

OPO. An organ procurement organization, which recovers deceased donor organs within its service area. See Plotting OPO service areas.

HRSA. The Health Resources and Services Administration, which oversees the OPTN and publishes the center and service-area maps sRtr downloads.

PSR. SRTR’s program-specific reports on each transplant program. Their technical methods define many of the outcomes sRtr follows.

DUA (data use agreement). The agreement under which a researcher receives SAFs. Real results leave your computer only as aggregate counts. See Share counts, never rows and how to share counts safely.
